purpose: Existing columns on lists this platform adopted rather than provisioned, which the flows filter on and which must carry a SharePoint index. An unindexed equality filter FAILS — it does not merely slow — once a list passes the 5,000-item view threshold, so these are correctness requirements, not optimisations. The browser provisioner sets them in a second pass after column creation; it reads each field first and skips one that is already indexed.
note: SharePoint allows at most 20 indexed columns per list, and indexing a column on a list already over the threshold can be refused. The provisioner reports the refusal rather than swallowing it. Sorting counts: past the threshold an $orderby on an unindexed column fails exactly as a $filter does, and the four targets added on 2026-09-02 include three that are sorts rather than filters.

DGO_SCHEDULED_SWEEP filters and sorts the due-date sweep on it. THIS ONE FAILED IN PRODUCTION: the first live run of AUTO_SCHEDULED_SWEEP returned status 400, 'exceeds the list view threshold', on Get_Due_Breached. Indexing is necessary and not sufficient — the sweep's query was also unbounded, and an indexed clause still has to return under 5,000 rows, which is why the flow now asks for a 30-day window rather than all history.

declaredOnNote: The date a target was added here. A target declared AFTER the newest recorded index run has no outcome because no run has reached it yet, which is a different thing from a run having skipped it — tests/sharepoint-field-spec.test.mjs distinguishes the two and reports the first as outstanding rather than as a failure. A target older than the newest run and still without an outcome remains a failure.
